hints: Focus on what hot concentrated acidified KMnO4 does to a C=C bond, it cleaves it completely and oxidises each end.
Count the carbons in the open chain product including the branch methyl, then compare with the total carbons in the ring options.
Join the ketone end and the acid end back together to reform the ring and see which carbons must have carried the methyl groups.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage rules**

Hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ breaks the $\text{C=C}$ bond. Each alkene carbon becomes a carbonyl carbon on its own.

$$\text{=CH}_2 \to \text{CO}_2, \quad \text{=CHR} \to \text{RCOOH}, \quad \text{=CR}_2 \to \text{RCOR}$$

**Analyse the given product**

The product is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Count carbons: 6 in the main chain plus 1 branch methyl = 7 carbons total.

Left end $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ is a ketone, so it came from $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)(R)}$. Right end $\text{COOH}$ is a carboxylic acid, so it came from $\text{CH(R)}$.

**Deduce ring size**

A cyclic alkene on cleavage opens to give one single chain with two carbonyl ends. Since the product has 7 carbons, the alkene must have 7 carbons.

Options A and B are dimethylcyclohexenes: $6+2=8$ carbons. Options C and D are dimethylcyclopentenes: $5+2=7$ carbons. So it must be C or D.

**Locate the methyl groups**

Join the two carbonyl carbons back with a double bond to close the ring: $\text{C}_a$ (ketone carbon) to $\text{C}_e$ (acid carbon).

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_a(-\text{C}_b)-=\text{C}_e(\text{H})-\text{C}_d-$$
$\text{C}_a$ has a $\text{CH}_3$ group and is joined to $\text{C}_b$ which itself carries a $\text{CH}_3$ group. So one methyl is on the double bond carbon and the second methyl is on the adjacent saturated carbon. This matches structure D.

options.A: 1,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene has 8 carbons. Cleavage would give an 8-carbon open chain, not the 7-carbon product observed. It would also place the methyls too far apart.
options.B: This dimethylcyclohexene also has 8 carbons. Its oxidative cleavage would give a longer dicarbonyl product with 8 carbons, so it cannot give the 6-carbon chain plus one branch seen here.
options.C: This is a dimethylcyclopentene with the correct carbon count, but the second methyl is on the wrong ring carbon, distant from the double bond. Cleavage would give $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)COOH}$, with the branch in a different position.
options.D: 1,5-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene has 7 carbons. The $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=}$ end gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ and the $\text{=CH-}$ end gives $\text{-COOH}$, while the $\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2-$ bridge stays intact to give exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.
